name: Zen-Zentrum Eisenbuch & Zen-Kloster Daihizan Fumonji
tradition: Soto Zen Buddhism (Japanese lineage via Antaiji and Eiheiji), practiced within a 'Heilsames Leben' (healing life) framework open to non-specialists
technique: Zazen (seated meditation), kinhin (walking meditation), samu (mindful work practice), sutra recitation, and Dharma talks
influences: Eiheiji Soto head monastery (Ekiho Miyazaki Zenji)
teacherAccess: Evening Dharma talks and Zendo introductions led by Fumon S. Nakagawa Roshi or senior Sangha members on most retreats; first-time practitioners can put questions to the Roshi directly
retreatOptions: Weekly open meditation evening; weekend Sesshin (3 nights); week-long Samu-, study- and 'Heilsames Leben' theme retreats; roughly two-week Nirvana- and Rohatsu-Sesshin for experienced students (by the Roshi's permission); month-long winter and summer Ango monastic retreats; short 'Kloster auf Zeit' stays
about: Zen-Zentrum Eisenbuch & Zen-Kloster Daihizan Fumonji is a Soto Zen monastery and retreat center set in a converted country inn in the wooded Holzland hills near Erlbach, Bavaria, about 110 km east of Munich. It was founded in 1996 by Fumon Shoju Nakagawa Roshi, a Japanese monk ordained by Tokugen Sakai Roshi and trained at Antaiji under Kosho Uchiyama Roshi and at the Soto head monastery Eiheiji, who envisioned the site as a 'Heilsames Leben' (healing life) path open to everyone, not only committed Zen trainees; the monastery was formally established in 2006 with the blessing of Eiheiji's 78th abbot, Ekiho Miyazaki Zenji. A resident monastic community and lay Sangha (Shobo-Kai) live on site and lead the year-round program of zazen, kinhin, samu (mindful work) and Dharma talks. Offerings range from a weekly open meditation evening and weekend Sesshin to week-long study and 'Heilsames Leben' courses, advanced multi-week Nirvana- and Rohatsu-Sesshin, and month-long winter and summer Ango monastic retreats. Meals are full-board, predominantly regional, organic and vegetarian, billed together with lodging separately from the course fee.
schedule: Typical retreat day runs roughly 5:00am-9:00pm with alternating periods of zazen, kinhin, samu (work practice), meals and an evening Dharma talk from the abbot; multi-day Sesshin are held mostly or entirely in silence.
cost: A fixed course fee (Kursgebühr) is charged per retreat (e.g. ~90 EUR for a weekend Sesshin, 120-240 EUR for week-long courses) and excludes accommodation and food, which are billed separately per night by room type; some community and self-catering Sesshins waive the course fee entirely, and the center also relies on voluntary dana at the close of courses.

pricePerDay.notes: Derived from the 3-night Wochenend-Sesshin (26-29 Mar 2026): course fee 90 EUR (~30 EUR/night) plus separately billed room-and-full-board rates ranging 103 EUR/night (shared double room, Zenhaus, shared bath) to 129 EUR/night (single room, private bath); combined total is roughly 133-159 EUR/night. A single-occupancy monk's apartment runs 150 EUR/night, and a 5 EUR/night surcharge applies for special diets.

foodNotes: Full board of predominantly regional, organic vegetarian meals is included in the nightly room rate; a 5 EUR/night surcharge applies for special dietary needs such as intolerances.
workNotes: Samu (mindful work in the house and garden) is built into the daily schedule of most retreats, from roughly 1-1.5 hours on a weekend Sesshin up to several hours a day on the dedicated Samu-Sesshin, alongside zazen and Dharma talks.
